**Resend:** The official docs list a Pro plan at $20/mo for 50,000 emails, with overage at $0.90 per 1,000 Free $0/mo 3,000; Pro $20/mo 50,000 $0.90. The "Pro 100k" tier is where the sources disagree. Some list it at $35/mo for 100,000 emails Pro is $20 a month for 50,000 emails (or $35 for 100,000), while others put 100,000 emails on the Scale plan at $90/mo Scale is $90/month for 100,000 emails/month. Several third-party guides describe a $30/mo add-on on the Scale plan (Dedicated IP add-on ($30/mo)), while others say dedicated IPs come with Enterprise, and one guide says they are available on Pro 100k and Enterprise tiers. Per Postmark's pricing text, they start at $50/month per IP and are only available on Pro plans or higher, for customers sending 300,000 emails per month or more. **Bottom line:** For 10,000 to 50,000 emails/month, Resend Pro ($20) and Postmark's entry plan (about $15 per third-party sources) are close in price. Resend's dedicated IP access starts at a lower volume and price, but the sources conflict on which tier includes it. Postmark's dedicated IP requires 300,000+ emails/month.

content.text:
**Recommendation: Postmark, if these emails are business-critical (password resets, receipts, login codes). Pick Resend if developer experience and a bigger free tier matter more to you.**

My direct fetches of both pricing pages were blocked. Everything below comes from search summaries and third-party sources, so confirm the numbers on the vendors' own pages before you commit.

**Pricing**

| | Resend | Postmark |
|---|---|---|
| Free tier | 3,000 emails/month | 100 emails/month |
| Entry paid plan | Pro at $20/month for 50,000 emails | About $15/month for 10,000 emails (one source says $10; unverified) |
| Overage | About $0.90 per 1,000 emails | I couldn't find a figure |
| Dedicated IP | Sources conflict: a $30/month add-on on Scale, Enterprise only, or Pro 100k | $50/month per IP, only for Pro plans and above, and for senders at 300,000+ emails/month |

- **Cost:** At low volume Resend is cheaper because its free tier is much larger. At 10,000–50,000 emails/month the two are close.
- **Dedicated IP:** Resend looks easier to reach, but the sources disagree on which plan includes it.

**Deliverability**
- Most reviewers rank Postmark ahead. They credit its strict sender vetting and its separation of transactional and broadcast mail into different streams.
- Resend is generally described as good but less proven. It was founded in 2023, and the main reason to pick it is its developer experience, including React Email templates.
- None of the sources I found had measured inbox-placement or bounce data for either service. The Postmark-favorable claims partly come from Postmark's own comparison page. So "Postmark is better" is a consensus of opinion, not tested fact.

**How to choose**
- **Postmark:** mail you can't afford to lose, and you're fine paying a little more.
- **Resend:** a startup or side project with low volume, a React stack, or a wish to start free.
- **Either one:** you can test the free tiers yourself. Send to Gmail, Outlook and Yahoo test inboxes with your own domain (SPF, DKIM and DMARC set up) and see where the mail lands.

Sources:
- [Resend vs Postmark comparison (Courier)](https://www.courier.com/integrations/compare/postmark-vs-resend)
- [Postmark's Resend comparison page](https://postmarkapp.com/compare/resend-alternative)
- [Resend vs SendGrid vs Postmark 2026 (Automation Atlas)](https://automationatlas.io/guides/resend-vs-sendgrid-vs-postmark-2026-comparison/)
- [Resend vs Postmark (Sequenzy)](https://sequenzy.com/versus/resend-vs-postmark)
- [Resend pricing docs](https://resend.com/docs/knowledge-base/what-is-resend-pricing.md)
- [Resend pricing 2026 (Automation Atlas)](https://automationatlas.io/answers/resend-pricing-explained-2026/)
- [Postmark pricing text](https://postmarkapp.com/pricing.txt)
- [Postmark pricing review (Email Software Insights)](https://www.emailsoftwareinsights.com/reviews/postmark/pricing/)
